Mariotronics

MARIO TEXTURE · FM-1 · 0.6
FM-1

Drag a knob vertically or focus it and use the arrow keys. Click the LCD to enlarge it. Play with A W S E D F T G Y H U J K. Z and X shift the octave.

First tape pass

Turn PRESETS to recall P01–P64. Hold SAVE for one second to open the name editor. K1 moves the cursor, K2 changes the letter, K3 rolls a tape-inspired name. Turn K4 left to erase a letter or right to select Delete Preset. PRESETS chooses the destination. Press SAVE to confirm or HOME to cancel. Tap SAVE for reverse. Guitar voice is on EDIT, K1.

Tap REC and play C and G. At the default delay, the notes return four seconds later. Tap REC during overdub to enter HOLD and play over the frozen pass. Tap REC again to resume overdubbing. Hold REC for 1.2 seconds to erase the tape. PLAY stops or resumes playback. SAVE reverses an existing loop in HOLD.

In EDIT, choose Sing for a rounded, sustained lead or Hollow for a stronger pick transient and more pronounced odd harmonics. EDIT sets drive, tape time and Tape/Loop mode. In Loop mode, tap REC again to set the phrase length, up to eight seconds. Recordings are held in RAM and clear at power-off. Use Power off and Power on to replay the startup animation.

Performance and effects

FX cycles through Off-Tape before Plate. K1 blends the first playback head (180 ms, default 25%) into the monitor during recording and overdubbing. LFO opens vibrato rate (Hz), depth (cents), wait and rise (0–1000 ms each). Wait sets how long a fresh note stays steady. Rise sets how gradually vibrato reaches full depth. Legato slides carry the vibrato forward. SEQ switches vibrato on or off. ARP switches two-note picking on and off. Hold two different notes to alternate them in the order played, with a repeating 3 + 3 + 2 accent. One held note plays normally. Set speed (3–16 notes per second), gate and accent on the ARP page. SEL → Phrasing controls legato glide. SEL opens Phrasing; press it again for Scales. Choose Chromatic, Dorian or Major and a root. For the modal centres of The Heavenly Music Corporation, try F-sharp Dorian, A major and D major. Eric Tamm’s analysis.

FX cycles through Compressor, Fuzz, Wah, Amp/Cab and Plate. The first four shape the guitar before recording. The stereo plate follows the sum of the live guitar and tape return, so its tail stays out of the recording. ENV opens the guitar’s attack, decay, sustain and release. HOME Swell shares the attack control.

Global MIDI and Bluetooth

Press GLO three times from Home for LIGHTS. K1 sets idle key brightness to OFF, HALF or FULL. Held notes light at maximum brightness. Press GLO for receive channel (Omni or 1–16), CC input, external sync and delay in quarter-note beats (1–16). With sync enabled, Tape follows a 24-PPQN MIDI clock up to eight seconds. Start rewinds and plays an existing tape or begins recording an empty one. Continue resumes; Stop halts the transport. With no clock the manual tape time takes over. Loop mode retains its recorded length.

Note On and Off include velocity and channel filtering. Program Change 0–63 recalls P01–P64. CC 1 controls vibrato depth, 7 amp volume, 11 tape send, 20 fuzz drive, 21 wah sweep, 22 feedback, 23 tape return and 91 plate mix. CC 120 and 123 release incoming notes on their channel.

On the FM-1, press GLO again for BLE MIDI. Turn K1 on. With Device at 0, press OCT+ to scan for ten seconds. Use K2 to select a discovered controller, then OCT+ to connect. USB MIDI and the TRS MIDI input also receive notes, controllers and clock. The FM-1 keyboard transmits notes over USB and the connected BLE link, on the selected channel (channel 1 in Omni). In the emulator, enable MIDI below and select a system input and, optionally, an output. For Bluetooth, pair your controller in the operating system first.

Time Lag Accumulator · Terry Riley

In Paris in 1963, Riley worked with a technician on a two-recorder system for Music for The Gift. The second machine’s playback signal returns to the first, where it mixes with the live input. At constant tape speed, increasing the distance between the heads lengthens the delay. In Tape mode, turn ALGORITHM while playing. Between four and eight seconds, the A77s move progressively apart.

Michael Peters · Reanimating Frippertronics · Time Lag Accumulator

Frippertronics · the 1979 setup

The Les Paul feeds the pedals and the left Revox. Tape crosses the recording head, reaches the playback head of the second A77 and winds onto the right reel. An audio cable returns the second machine’s output to the first. At 19 cm/s, 76 cm between heads gives a four-second delay.

Install on FM-1

Connect one FM-1 via USB and open this page in Chrome or Edge. Installing replaces the current firmware. The firmware package is included. This build has been tested in emulation.
